text:
Marathon Petroleum stock edged up 0.26% today to close at $478.14, capping a two-week surge of 13.2% driven by sharp gains in crude oil prices and refinery profitability. U.S. crude rose above $101 per barrel as Iran escalated attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping chokepoint; Brent crude touched $110, widening the gap between U.S. and global oil prices. Refineries are running at 93.5% capacity, near maximum, which means Marathon captures more of the profit margin between buying crude and selling gasoline and diesel—especially valuable when crude prices spike suddenly.

The two-week rally reflects how geopolitical tension directly benefits U.S. oil refiners. Iran's actions tighten global crude supplies and push shipping costs higher, which makes the physical delivery of oil more expensive; analysts note the true cost to move crude can run $30–$40 per barrel above the spot price. Marathon's refineries benefit from this widening gap—they can buy U.S. crude at $101 but sell products into a global market where Brent trades at $126.55, and refinery utilization near 94% means the company is running flat-out to capture that spread.
